# Tip-closure fixture: naca2412_tip_r60_t3_s60.stl

## Description
A tapered NACA 2412 wing built exactly like the taper fixture (straight leading edge, linear chord change, 2 exact stations) but with a much smaller tip chord -- 60 mm at the root down to 3 mm at the tip over 60 mm of span -- so the section area genuinely collapses toward zero rather than merely narrowing. This is the M5 pattern-shutdown case: any structural pattern (e.g. a web) that assumes a minimum section thickness must stop being placed before the tip, not fail or silently corrupt when the section gets too thin to hold it.

## Origin convention
Same root-bounding-box-centring convention as the taper fixture. Z is spanwise, root at Z=0, tip at Z=60 mm.

## Exact dimensions
- NACA designation: 2412 (m=0.02, p=0.4, t=0.12)
- Root chord: 60 mm
- Tip chord: 3 mm
- Span: 60 mm
- Taper: linear, leading edge at fixed local X (straight LE), same construction as the taper fixture
- SHA-256 (STL): 63b0c6fe849f6bf3a0a7a55ff73b57bd5be596de3be6292149957bc9a91fef2e
- Points per surface: 120 (cosine-spaced; outline vertex count 238)
- Stations: 2 (root, tip) -- geometrically exact for a linear taper
- Triangles: 948 (476 side wall + 472 cap)
- Format: binary STL, deterministic fixed ASCII header, no timestamps

## Local thickness by spanwise station, and where pattern shutdown must occur
Local max thickness scales linearly with chord for a fixed NACA thickness digit, so it falls below the 1 mm default skin margin at:
- chord = 8.3350 mm
- Z = 54.3842 mm (90.64% of span from the root)

Any structural pattern generator using this fixture must close out before Z=54.3842 mm -- the table below brackets that point with explicit stations on both sides.

## Purpose
M5 fixture: area collapses toward zero. Requires an explicit pattern shutdown / closure strategy rather than assuming a web fits everywhere between root and tip.

Generated by `python tools/make_fixtures.py tip --naca 2412 --root-chord 60 --tip-chord 3 --span 60 --points 120 --skin-margin 1`.
